title: Binary Tree Common Ancestor
statement:
Find the lowest node in a general binary tree that contains two given nodes in its subtree.

Contract
- `root`, `first`, and `second` are node references from the same node type. A node may be its own ancestor.
- Return the lowest common ancestor by object identity when both requested nodes are present in the tree rooted at `root`.
- Return null if the tree is empty or either requested node is not present. The tree is not necessarily a search tree, and values may repeat.

Examples
`lowestCommonAncestor(root, root.left, root.right).value` in tree `[3, 5, 1, 6, 2, 0, 8]` => `3`
`lowestCommonAncestor(root, root.left, root.left.right).value` in that tree => `5`
`lowestCommonAncestor(null, new TreeNode(1), new TreeNode(2))` => `null`
hints: Ignore binary-search ordering; this is a general tree.
A recursive search can report whether each target appears under the current node.
Only return an ancestor after proving both targets were found under the root. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(h) stack space.
inputSyntax: Input: two target values followed by the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: 5 1 [3, 5, 1, 6, 2, 0, 8]
